title: 2001 HMMT February Geometry Problem 9
statement: Parallelogram \(A E C F\) is inscribed in square \(A B C D\). It is reflected across diagonal \(A C\) to form another parallelogram \(A E^{\prime} C F^{\prime}\). The region common to both parallelograms has area \(m\) and perimeter \(n\). Compute the value of \(\frac{m}{n^{2}}\) if \(A F: A D=1: 4\).

solutions.text: By symmetry, the region is a rhombus, AXCY, centered at the center of the square, \(O\). Consider isoceles right triangle \(A C D\). By the technique of mass points, we find that \(D O: Y O=7: 1\). Therefore, the rhombus is composed of four triangles, whose sides are in the ratio \(1: 7: 5 \sqrt{2}\). The perimeter of the rhombus is \(20 \sqrt{2} N\), and the area is \(14 N^{2}\). The required ratio is thus \(\frac{7}{400}\).
